doc.title: Melba Liston — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Listening to Annie's Dance
summary: They hear Annie's Dance with Charli Persip, written while the band worked at Birdland, before the tour.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: That’s good then. That was good. So we’ve seen two sides of you. Now we’re going to see another side of your writing. We’re going to try another one of Melba’s arrangements with Dizzy’s band, a little something different. It’s – she calls it Annie’s Dance, and it’s a play on the semi-classical tune called Anitra’s Dance. [The music plays.] That is really a beautiful arrangement on that.
It’s still good.
Yes, it’s still good. The interplay between the sections, and when Charli Persip with his – he sounds like somebody tiptoeing on the drums, tap-dancing or something. Your shadings and everything.
Yeah, that’s good.
Did you write – you wrote that before you guys went over, right?
Oh yeah. We were at Birdland.
That’s where you tried it out? You tried it out at Birdland?
I didn’t try out.
No, what I mean, you try something out before you go over . . .
No.
You played it. I mean you played it.
We were . . .
Working there.
. . . working there, wherever we were, before – we didn’t know about . . .
Birdland? The tour?
. . . when I wrote it.
Oh. Okay.
Some things you just – you got to write some things. So he told me to write some things, so I . . .
That’s one of the things you wrote.
Yeah.
